📄 Iran: Zionist regime poses gravest threat to Lebanon’s independence, stability

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran's Foreign Ministry has strongly condemned the Israeli aggression against Lebanon, stating that the attacks—coinciding with the country's Independence Day— show the Zionist regime poses the greatest threat to its independence, territorial integrity, and stability.

In a statement on Wednesday, the ministry denounced Israeli airstrikes and shelling across various areas of southern Lebanon, as well as the destruction of civilian infrastructure in the country, reaffirming the Arab country's inherent right to defend its sovereignty and territorial integrity.
​
The statement said the Israeli military escalation, occurring while the Lebanese people were commemorating the anniversary of their independence, constitutes a flagrant violation of the UN Charter and the November 2024 ceasefire agreement.
​
It noted that such aggressive actions are the stark reality of the Zionist enemy, which represents the gravest threat to Lebanon's independence, territorial integrity, security, and stability.
​
The Foreign Ministry also highlighted Israeli atrocities and crimes in violation of international law in Gaza, the West Bank, Syria, and other regional nations, demanding a firm response from the United Nations and the international community.
​
Slamming the United States as Israel’s main backer and accomplice in preventing effective international action against the regime, the ministry also pointed to the UN Security Council's inaction over continued Israeli violations.
​
It warned that the UN Security Council’s failure to act regarding Israel's occupation of vast areas of Lebanon and its continued aggression not only undermines the credibility of the world body but also emboldens the regime to keep violating international law.
​
The statement further condemned US interference in Lebanon’s internal affairs, warning that Washington's efforts to establish mechanisms lacking national consensus are aimed at paving the way for the Zionist regime's sinister and expansionist agenda.
​
In closing, the Foreign Ministry praised the Lebanese people’s resilience in the face of Israeli aggression and reaffirmed Iran's support for Lebanon in defending its independence, national sovereignty, and territorial integrity.

The United States has escalated its technological confrontation with China by placing seven Asian companies on its trade blacklist over alleged links to the diversion of advanced American semiconductor technology.

The restrictions target companies operating in Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand, including Megaspeed. Washington suspects that these networks may have helped China gain access to advanced Nvidia chips despite existing export controls.

The affected companies will now face strict licensing requirements when seeking access to American technologies. Alibaba has disputed allegations involving its subsidiary.

The bigger picture: Washington is no longer trying merely to restrict direct semiconductor exports to China. It is attempting to control the entire international supply chain through which Beijing could obtain advanced computing power.

But there is a strategic paradox. The tighter America's restrictions become, the stronger China's incentive to develop its own semiconductor industry and reduce dependence on Western suppliers.

The real battle may not be about who manufactures the most powerful chip today, but who controls the technology, infrastructure and supply chains of tomorrow.
